arguments.title: Calculus: Secant to Derivative
arguments.opening_prompt: Help me connect secant slopes to derivatives.

text: I inspected your live settings, prompt segments, and knowledge graph (`Slope`), and prepared a 1-click Teaching launch card above.
Let's begin by checking how you think about rate of change.

arguments.question: What does the slope of a secant line between two points on $y = f(x)$ represent?

options.label: The average rate of change of $f$ between those two points
The instantaneous derivative at the midpoint
The area under the curve between the points

arguments.explanation: A secant line connects $(x_1, f(x_1))$ and $(x_2, f(x_2))$, so its slope is the average rate of change.
